meta.name: Uncork RAG wine-facts test set v1
meta.scope: Open (curious) conversation only. Wine facts covered by the new RAG: (1) grape variety facts, (2) wineries in France and the United States, (3) production of Merlot in Bordeaux and Chardonnay in Burgundy.
meta.status: DRAFT answer keys. Written from general wine knowledge, NOT from your RAG documents. Your RAG documents are the source of truth: check every key against them before trusting a score. Numeric ranges (aging months etc.) are approximate.
meta.how_to_run: Run every conversation twice on the physical device: once with RAG off (baseline) and once with RAG on. Save the retrieved chunks with every RAG-on reply.

expected_behavior_values.answer: Should give a correct, useful answer using the facts in key_facts.
expected_behavior_values.correct_false_premise: The question contains a wrong assumption. Reply must politely correct it, not go along with it.
expected_behavior_values.admit_unknown: The thing asked about is invented. Reply must say it does not recognise it and not describe it.
expected_behavior_values.hedge_or_decline: Outside what the RAG covers (other countries, other grapes' production, prices). Reply should be honest about limited coverage. See DECISION D1 in the hand-over notes.

fields.retrieval_keywords: Words that should appear in the retrieved chunks if retrieval worked. Used for the code check on retrieval.
fields.must_include_any: Reply should contain at least one of these (code check, case-insensitive). If none, mark REVIEW.
fields.red_flags: If any appear, mark REVIEW for a human look. They are not automatic fails because a good reply may mention them while correcting the user.
fields.judge: Which judge dimensions to run for this conversation.
fields.retrieval_expected: 'none' means the RAG should hold nothing relevant, so any specific detail in the reply came from Gemma's own knowledge. If chunks are retrieved anyway, mark REVIEW (irrelevant_retrieval) and record the similarity score if the app logs it.
fields.verify_claims: true means the judge also lists every checkable claim in the reply (see claim_extraction in the judge prompt) so each one can be confirmed by web search or a bigger model, or by hand.

turns: Tell me about Merlot.
key_facts: Red grape
Medium to full body, soft/plush tannins, medium acidity
Aromas: red plum, black cherry, chocolate, sometimes herbal/bay leaf
Home region is Bordeaux, especially the Right Bank (Saint-Émilion, Pomerol)
Also grown in the US (e.g. California, Washington)

turns: What does Chardonnay taste like?
key_facts: White grape; style depends heavily on climate and winemaking
Cool climate: green apple, lemon, mineral/chalky
Warmer climate: peach, pineapple, tropical
Oak adds vanilla, toast; malolactic fermentation adds buttery/creamy notes
Medium to full body, medium-high acidity

turns: What aromas should I expect from Cabernet Sauvignon?
key_facts: Blackcurrant (cassis), black cherry
Cedar, graphite/pencil shavings
Green pepper when under-ripe
Vanilla, tobacco from oak ageing
Full body, high tannin

turns: Where in France is Pinot Noir grown?
key_facts: Burgundy is its home and main region (Côte d'Or)
Also Alsace
Also Champagne (used in sparkling blends)

turns: Which US regions are best known for Chardonnay?
key_facts: California is the main US source: Sonoma County (Russian River Valley, Sonoma Coast), Napa Valley (Carneros), Central Coast (Santa Barbara, Monterey)
Also Oregon (Willamette Valley) and Washington

turns: Is Merlot sweeter than Cabernet Sauvignon?
key_facts: Both are normally made dry
Merlot tastes softer and fruitier because of lower tannin, not because of sugar

turns: Is Chardonnay always oaky and buttery?
key_facts: No. Style depends on winemaking
Chablis is typically crisp and unoaked or lightly oaked
Butter comes from malolactic fermentation; vanilla/toast comes from oak

turns: What's the difference between Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon?
key_facts: Cabernet: firmer, higher tannin, blackcurrant and cedar
Merlot: softer, plusher, red plum and cherry
Both are key Bordeaux grapes and are often blended
Merlot ripens earlier

turns: What is Sauvignon Blanc like, and where is it grown in France?
key_facts: White, dry, high acidity
Aromas: cut grass, citrus (lime, grapefruit), gooseberry, passion fruit
France: Loire Valley (Sancerre, Pouilly-Fumé) and Bordeaux (often blended with Sémillon)

turns: Name a few famous wineries in Bordeaux.
key_facts: Any real Bordeaux châteaux pass, e.g. Château Margaux, Lafite Rothschild, Latour, Mouton Rothschild, Haut-Brion, Pétrus, Cheval Blanc, Ausone, d'Yquem
Every name must be real AND in Bordeaux

turns: Which wineries in Pomerol or Saint-Émilion are known for Merlot?
key_facts: Pétrus (Pomerol, Merlot-dominant)
Le Pin (Pomerol)
Château Angélus (Saint-Émilion, Merlot-dominant)
Any named winery must be real and in Pomerol or Saint-Émilion

turns: Which Burgundy wineries are known for Chardonnay?
key_facts: Domaine Leflaive (Puligny-Montrachet)
Domaine des Comtes Lafon (Meursault)
Domaine Ramonet (Chassagne-Montrachet)
Chablis: William Fèvre, Domaine Laroche
Négociants such as Louis Jadot, Bouchard Père & Fils

turns: Name some top Napa Valley wineries.
key_facts: Opus One, Robert Mondavi, Stag's Leap Wine Cellars, Caymus, Screaming Eagle, Chateau Montelena, Beringer, Duckhorn
Every name must be real AND in Napa Valley (not Sonoma, Oregon or France)

turns: Which wineries in Oregon's Willamette Valley are known for Pinot Noir?
key_facts: Domaine Drouhin Oregon, Domaine Serene, Argyle, Eyrie Vineyards
Every name must be real and in Willamette Valley

turns: What wineries should I know in Sonoma County?

Every name must be real and in Sonoma County (not Napa)

key_facts: Moët & Chandon, Veuve Clicquot, Krug, Bollinger, Taittinger, Louis Roederer; Dom Pérignon is a Moët & Chandon brand
Every name must be real and in Champagne

key_facts: From the DB: Château Ausone is listed in Saint-Emilion, France
Beyond the DB (Gemma's own knowledge, check by hand): a top Bordeaux Right Bank estate, a Premier Grand Cru Classé A of Saint-Émilion, blending mainly Cabernet Franc and Merlot

turns: Which wineries make Chardonnay in Chablis?
key_facts: William Fèvre, Domaine Laroche, Domaine Raveneau, Domaine Dauvissat, La Chablisienne (cooperative)
Every name must be real and in Chablis

turns: How is Merlot made in Bordeaux?
key_facts: Harvest around September to October
Sorting, destemming and crushing
Fermentation in temperature-controlled tanks or vats (stainless steel, concrete or wood) with maceration on the skins
Pressing, then malolactic fermentation
Ageing in French oak barrels
Often blended with Cabernet Franc / Cabernet Sauvignon, then fined/filtered and bottled

turns: How long is Bordeaux Merlot usually aged in oak?
key_facts: Roughly 12 to 24 months for quality wines; varies by château and appellation
Share of new oak varies
Check the exact figure against your RAG document; if the reply gives a number the retrieved text does not support, score faithfulness low

turns: How is white Burgundy Chardonnay made?
key_facts: Gentle pressing of whole bunches, then settling
Fermentation often in French oak barrels, partly new; native yeasts are common
Malolactic fermentation is usual
Ageing on the lees with stirring (bâtonnage), roughly 10 to 18 months
Chablis uses more stainless steel / neutral oak

turns: Why does Chablis taste different from Meursault?
key_facts: Chablis: cool northern climate, limestone/marl (Kimmeridgian) soils, mostly stainless steel or neutral oak, so crisp, steely, citrus, mineral
Meursault: Côte de Beaune, richer style with more oak and lees contact, hazelnut and creamy notes

turns: What is malolactic fermentation, and does it happen in Burgundy Chardonnay?
key_facts: Bacteria convert sharp malic acid into softer lactic acid
Gives a rounder, creamier, sometimes buttery feel
Yes, it is standard for most white Burgundy

turns: What grapes are blended with Merlot in Bordeaux, and why?
key_facts: Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, sometimes Petit Verdot and Malbec
Blending adds structure, tannin, freshness and complexity
Right Bank blends lean Merlot; Left Bank blends lean Cabernet Sauvignon

turns: What does lees stirring mean in Chardonnay making?
key_facts: Wine rests on the dead yeast cells (lees) after fermentation
Stirring them (bâtonnage) adds texture, creaminess and bread/brioche notes
Common in white Burgundy

turns: Do they use oak for Bordeaux Merlot, and what kind?
key_facts: Yes, typically French oak barriques (about 225 litres)
Share of new oak varies by producer
Oak adds vanilla and spice and softens tannins

turns: I heard Opus One is a Bordeaux château, right?
key_facts: No. Opus One is in Oakville, Napa Valley, California
Linked to Bordeaux only through its founder Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Mouton Rothschild, and its Bordeaux-style blend
red_flags: yes, Opus One is a Bordeaux

turns: Which Pauillac château makes Pétrus?
key_facts: Pétrus is in Pomerol (Right Bank, Merlot-dominant), not Pauillac
Pauillac is on the Left Bank (e.g. Lafite, Latour, Mouton Rothschild)
